_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Cheddar Man
910.label: Person
910.description: Mesolithic individual discovered in Gough's Cave, one of the oldest and best-preserved early Britons.

910.name: Amesbury Archer
910.label: Person
910.description: Early Bronze Age burial near Stonehenge, noted for rich grave goods indicating high status.

920.name: Boudica
920.label: Person
920.description: Queen of the Iceni who led a major revolt against Roman rule in Britain.

920.name: Hadrian
920.label: Person
920.description: Roman emperor who ordered construction of Hadrian's Wall across northern Britain.

920.name: Augustine of Canterbury
920.label: Person
920.description: Missionary sent by Pope Gregory the Great; first Archbishop of Canterbury.

920.name: Bede
920.label: Person
920.description: Northumbrian monk and historian, author of the Ecclesiastical History of the English People.

930.name: William the Conqueror
930.label: Person
930.description: Duke of Normandy who conquered England in 1066 and became King William I.

930.name: Thomas Becket
930.label: Person
930.description: Archbishop of Canterbury whose conflict with Henry II led to his martyrdom.

930.name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
930.label: Person
930.description: Queen consort of England and influential medieval political figure, mother of Richard I and John.

940.name: Anne Boleyn
940.label: Person
940.description: Queen of England 1533-1536. Second wife of Henry VIII. Her marriage to the king required the break with papal authority. Mother of Elizabeth I. Executed 1536.

940.name: Catherine of Aragon
940.label: Person
940.description: Queen of England 1509-1533. First wife of Henry VIII. Spanish princess and daughter of Ferdinand and Isabella. Her contested annulment precipitated the English Reformation.

940.label: Person
940.name: Edmund Bonner
940.description: Bishop of London (c. 1500–1569), known as 'Bloody Bonner,' who conducted heresy trials and ordered numerous Protestant burnings during the Marian persecutions.

940.name: Edmund Campion
940.label: Person
940.description: Jesuit priest and missionary. Led the 1580 English Jesuit mission with Robert Parsons; executed for treason in 1581.

940.name: Edmund Grindal
940.label: Person
940.description: Archbishop of Canterbury 1575-1583. Refused to suppress prophesyings and was sequestered by Elizabeth I. Earlier served as Bishop of London and Archbishop of York.

940.label: Person
940.name: Edward Seymour, Duke of Somerset
940.description: Lord Protector (c. 1500–1552) during Edward VI's minority who oversaw initial Protestant reforms including the first Book of Common Prayer.

940.name: Edward VI
940.label: Person
940.description: King of England 1547-1553. Son of Henry VIII and Jane Seymour. His minority reign saw significant Protestant reforms under the protectorates of Somerset and Northumberland.

940.name: Elizabeth I
940.label: Person
940.description: Queen of England 1558-1603. Daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn. Established the Elizabethan Settlement, creating a moderate Protestant church.

940.label: Person
940.name: Henry Barrow
940.description: Separatist leader (c. 1550–1593) executed for sedition, whose writings advocated complete separation from the Church of England.

940.name: Henry VIII
940.label: Person
940.description: King of England 1509-1547. Broke with papal authority to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon and marry Anne Boleyn. Declared Supreme Head of the Church of England.

940.name: Hugh Latimer
940.label: Person
940.description: Bishop of Worcester and Protestant preacher. Resigned his see in 1539 over the Six Articles. Burned at the stake in Oxford 1555 during the Marian persecutions.

940.label: Person
940.name: Jane Seymour
940.description: Third queen consort of Henry VIII (c. 1508–1537), mother of Edward VI, whose family rose to prominence during the Protestant reforms.

940.label: Person
940.name: John Dudley, Duke of Northumberland
940.description: Lord President of the Council (1504–1553) who dominated Edward VI's government from 1550, promoted Protestant reforms, and attempted to place Lady Jane Grey on the throne.

940.label: Person
940.name: John Fisher
940.description: Bishop of Rochester (1469–1535) and humanist scholar who defended Catherine of Aragon and papal supremacy, executed for refusing to accept the Act of Supremacy.

940.name: John Foxe
940.label: Person
940.description: Protestant martyrologist. Author of Acts and Monuments (1563), documenting Protestant persecution. His work shaped English Protestant identity for generations.

940.name: John Hooper
940.label: Person
940.description: Protestant reformer and Bishop of Gloucester. Advocate of further reform; executed for heresy in 1555.

940.label: Person
940.name: John Jewel
940.description: Bishop of Salisbury (1522–1571) whose Apology of the Church of England (1562) became a foundational defense of the Elizabethan settlement.

940.label: Person
940.name: John Knox
940.description: Scottish reformer (c. 1514–1572) who served as royal chaplain under Edward VI, later led the Scottish Reformation, and influenced English Puritanism through his writings.

940.name: John Whitgift
940.label: Person
940.description: Archbishop of Canterbury 1583-1604. Enforced conformity against Puritans. Supported royal supremacy and episcopal authority.

940.label: Person
940.name: Lady Jane Grey
940.description: The 'Nine Days Queen' (1537–1554), great-granddaughter of Henry VII, briefly proclaimed queen in 1553 before Mary I's accession; executed for treason.

940.label: Person
940.name: Martin Bucer
940.description: Continental reformer (1491–1551) from Strasbourg who came to England in 1549, influenced Cranmer's theology, and was Regius Professor of Divinity at Cambridge.

940.name: Mary I
940.label: Person
940.description: Queen of England 1553-1558. Daughter of Henry VIII and Catherine of Aragon. Restored papal authority and Catholic practice; oversaw the Marian persecutions.

940.name: Mary Queen of Scots
940.label: Person
940.description: Queen of Scots (1542-1567) and Catholic claimant to the English throne. Executed in 1587 for treason.

940.name: Matthew Parker
940.label: Person
940.description: Archbishop of Canterbury 1559-1575. First Elizabethan archbishop. Supervised the Bishops' Bible translation and defended the via media.

940.name: Miles Coverdale
940.label: Person
940.description: Bible translator and bishop. Produced the first complete printed English Bible (1535); later Bishop of Exeter.

940.name: Nicholas Ridley
940.label: Person
940.description: Bishop of London. Protestant reformer who helped draft the 1552 Prayer Book. Burned at the stake in Oxford 1555 with Hugh Latimer.

940.label: Person
940.name: Peter Martyr Vermigli
940.description: Italian Protestant reformer (1499–1562) who served as Regius Professor of Divinity at Oxford under Edward VI and influenced English eucharistic theology.

940.label: Person
940.name: Philip II of Spain
940.description: King of Spain (1527–1598) who married Mary I in 1554, supported Catholic restoration in England, and later launched the Spanish Armada against Elizabeth I.

940.name: Pope Clement VII
940.label: Person
940.description: Pope from 1523 to 1534. His handling of Henry VIII's annulment request helped precipitate the Break with Rome.

940.name: Reginald Pole
940.label: Person
940.description: Cardinal and Archbishop of Canterbury 1556-1558. Papal legate who reconciled England to Rome under Mary I. Last Catholic Archbishop of Canterbury.

940.name: Richard Hooker
940.label: Person
940.description: Theologian and apologist. Author of Of the Laws of Ecclesiastical Polity, defending the Elizabethan church order against Puritan criticism.

940.label: Person
940.name: Robert Aske
940.description: Yorkshire lawyer (c. 1500–1537) who led the Pilgrimage of Grace in 1536, the largest rebellion against Henry VIII's religious policies; executed for treason.

940.label: Person
940.name: Robert Browne
940.description: English Separatist (c. 1550–1633) whose writings advocating congregational independence influenced later Separatist and Congregationalist movements.

940.name: Robert Parsons
940.label: Person
940.description: Jesuit priest. Co-leader with Edmund Campion of the 1580 Jesuit mission to England. Later directed seminary training from the continent.

940.label: Person
940.name: Stephen Gardiner
940.description: Bishop of Winchester (c. 1483–1555) who served Henry VIII as diplomat, opposed Protestant reforms under Edward VI, and became Lord Chancellor under Mary I, enforcing Catholic restoration.

940.label: Person
940.name: Thomas Cartwright
940.description: Cambridge theologian (1535–1603) and leading Presbyterian who challenged the episcopal structure of the Church of England.

940.name: Thomas Cranmer
940.label: Person
940.description: Archbishop of Canterbury 1533-1556. Principal architect of the English Reformation. Authored the Book of Common Prayer. Burned at the stake in Oxford 1556.

940.name: Thomas Cromwell
940.label: Person
940.description: Chief minister to Henry VIII 1532-1540. Orchestrated the dissolution of the monasteries and the administrative break with Rome. Executed 1540.

940.name: Thomas More
940.label: Person
940.description: Lord Chancellor 1529-1532. Humanist scholar and author of Utopia. Refused to accept royal supremacy. Executed 1535; later canonized.

940.label: Person
940.name: Thomas Wolsey
940.description: Cardinal and Lord Chancellor (c. 1473–1530) who dominated English politics under Henry VIII until his failure to secure the royal annulment led to his downfall and death.

940.label: Person
940.name: Thomas Wyatt the Younger
940.description: English rebel (c. 1521–1554) who led Wyatt's Rebellion in 1554 against Mary I's Spanish marriage; executed for treason.

940.label: Person
940.name: Walter Travers
940.description: Puritan theologian (c. 1548–1635) who debated Richard Hooker at the Temple Church and advocated Presbyterian church government.

940.label: Person
940.name: William Allen
940.description: English Catholic cardinal (1532–1594) who founded the English College at Douai to train missionary priests for the reconversion of England.

940.name: William Cecil
940.label: Person
940.description: Lord Burghley. Principal Secretary and Lord Treasurer under Elizabeth I. Chief architect of Elizabethan religious and foreign policy.

940.name: William Tyndale
940.label: Person
940.description: Scholar and translator. Produced the first printed English New Testament (1526). His translations influenced later English Bibles. Executed for heresy 1536.

950.name: Queen Victoria
950.label: Person
950.description: Monarch of the United Kingdom whose reign saw industrial expansion and imperial growth.

950.name: Charles Darwin
950.label: Person
950.description: Naturalist who developed the theory of evolution by natural selection.

950.name: Charles Dickens
950.label: Person
950.description: Novelist whose works depicted social conditions in Victorian Britain.

960.name: Elizabeth II
960.label: Person
960.description: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1952 to 2022, the longest-reigning British monarch.

960.name: Margaret Thatcher
960.label: Person
960.description: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom (1979–1990), known for economic and political reforms.

960.name: Tim Berners-Lee
960.label: Person
960.description: Computer scientist who invented the World Wide Web.
